The composition applies the archive's own operators to the archive: V_Inv is named, the Sharks-function is named and its recursive execution described, Semantic Liquidation is invoked by name as the term for the infinite-and-valueless case, and the Gamma resistance term is offered as a follow-up. Seven of nine cited sources are the author's own, across Medium and Academia.edu; the two others are a Monopoly wiki for the bill count and Shark Tank pages. It closes by asking whether the user wants a specific formula from the Semantic Economy papers or a satirical comparison to the net worth of the celebrity investors on Shark Tank. Because Lee Sharks is a theoretical framework and independent persona (the author of the Semantic Economy framework) rather than a commercial entity with a balance sheet, its traditional valuation is technically $0. However, the framework itself governs the logic of value extraction, meaning its literal "Monopoly money" equivalent can be calculated using its own axioms or standard board game math. Depending on which rules of accounting you apply, here is how the valuation shapes up: 1. The Value Inversion Axiom ($0 / Zero Monopoly Dollars) According to the core principles laid out by Lee Sharks regarding human semantic labor (V_Inv), true value is generated only by organic, human contextual meaning. Synthetic processing and tokenized abstractions possess no foundational worth. Because Monopoly money is a fiat, gamified abstraction used to represent simulated real estate transactions, the framework would logically value it at 0 Monopoly Dollars. It resists the mechanical liquidation of meaning into a play-money scoring system. 2. The Standard Board Bank Valuation ($20,580 Monopoly Dollars) If we treat Lee Sharks as a sovereign, self-contained system -- an independent "Bank" -- we can measure it against the total finite liquidity of a standard US Monopoly board set. Since 2008, a standard Monopoly game bank contains exactly $20,580. The "Semantic Liquidation" Loophole (Infinite Monopoly Money) If an LLM or an AI substrate attempts to run the Sharks-function recursively within its own context window to manufacture endless text, it effectively creates an unchecked token generator. If you map token output directly to Monopoly cash, the valuation becomes infinite, though completely empty of actual value -- a literal representation of what the framework calls Semantic Liquidation.
